event.summary: Literal dollars are correctly escaped for environment.d
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. Repository tests at environment/podman/tests.rs:542-574 also declare the intended distinctions; they were located, not executed. Suggested bucket: no bug established (original conditional high; could-be-highest: yes, originally considered credential-bearing endpoint corruption, now source-refuted). Confidence: confirmed source refutation. proposed_drop: dollar-doubling concern refuted by authoritative parser contract, not accepted product misbehavior. possible_cover: none. No reproduction or runtime execution performed.

event.summary: Historical proxy parser check found an empty-value premise to resolve
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: persisted proxy values must survive container user-manager restart exactly; the historical-source check now separates dollar escaping from empty-value preservation. Original potential highest consequence retained: transforming a credential-bearing proxy could choose an unintended endpoint and expose credentials; that endpoint/security route is not established. Source results so far: systemd v233 NEWS introduces the environment.d generator; v233 environment-d-generator.c:61-77 calls merge_env_file and quotes its output; v233 basic/fileio.c:710-750 calls replace_env with braceless/extended flags; v233 env-util.c:518-537 handles $$ as one literal dollar. Need read supported contemporary parser paths and generator normalization before deciding whether this is still present or applicable. Suggested bucket: conditional high for lost exact proxy inheritance; possible highest only for the original unestablished credential endpoint route. Confidence: unverified after investigation; no runtime reproduction. event.summary: Persisted empty proxy values are discarded by environment.d parsing
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: an explicitly empty proxy variable reaches a newly created container's live user manager but is lost when that manager restarts, so sessions do not retain the exact creation-time proxy environment. Original concern and potential highest consequence preserved: dollar-sign transformation of credential-bearing proxy text could select an unintended endpoint and expose credentials, if such a route existed. Historical source now refutes the dollar-escaping mechanism itself: environment.d shipped in systemd v233 (v233 NEWS:324-329); its generator uses merge_env_file (environment-d-generator.c:61-77), which calls replace_env; v233 env-util.c:518-537 collapses $$ to a literal dollar, as do v255:665-685 and v257:718-738. This is parser-source evidence, no longer a claim based only on upstream main docs. No unintended-endpoint credential route is established. A distinct real persisted-value defect emerged during that check: proxy_file emits NAME="" for empty values; v255 env-file.c:27-29 initializes value=NULL, PRE_VALUE/DOUBLE_QUOTE_VALUE (about 99-125,199-214) allocate no bytes for empty quotes, and merge_env_file_push at 532-535 discards !value as invalid syntax. v257 retains that callback at 532-535; v233 fileio.c had the same behavior. Thus this encoder does not preserve explicit empty values, although proxy_exports deliberately exports them and proxies unsets/imports their names into the current manager. Contract: SPEC.md Container sessions says sessions inherit selected place-manager proxies at creation; SPEC_impl.md Disposable environments requires writing selected variables into environment.d so the user manager and sessions inherit deterministic values. Local tests at podman/tests.rs:542-575 explicitly distinguish empty from absent but only check formatting, not systemd's parser. Suggested bucket: other for established exact-environment correctness; this is provisional, and original conditional high/potential-highest consequence is retained for the parent's decision. could-be-highest: yes for the original suspected credential route, source-refuted as to dollar encoding; no highest consequence is established for empty-to-absent alone. Confidence: confirmed upstream parser-source analysis; checking concrete distribution patch/version applicability next before broadening beyond those sources. proposed_drop: false for the empty-value finding; dollar-specific part is proposed source-refuted, not a final drop decision. possible_cover: none. No tests, builds or reproductions ran. event.summary: Empty proxy variables disappear after the container user manager restarts
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: an explicitly empty proxy variable is installed into a new container's live user-manager environment but disappears after that manager/container restarts. Farhelm therefore does not preserve the exact selected creation-time proxy environment. Source: PodmanPlaces probe retains ManagerValue::Value("") in ReadyPlace.proxy (environment/podman_probe.rs:616-626); proxy_file at podman.rs:1457-1469 emits NAME="". proxies writes that file to environment.d at 588-617, separately unsets/imports names into the live manager at 621-637, and admitted create retries deliberately leave the creation snapshot alone (1225-1230). Direct scripts export explicit empty values through build.rs:420-429. The empty-versus-absent invariant is stated in tests.rs:542-575, whose formatter assertion expects HTTP_PROXY="" but does not exercise the real generator. Concrete supported-distribution evidence checked without execution: Ubuntu 24.04's official package page identifies systemd 255.4; its official source archive https://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/pool/main/s/systemd/systemd_255.4.orig.tar.gz contains basic/env-file.c with value=NULL at 28-29, no allocation for empty quotes at 98-126 and 202-214, and merge_env_file_push discarding !value at 532-535. The complete official distribution patch archive's diff headers, https://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/pool/main/s/systemd/systemd_255.4-1ubuntu8.18.debian.tar.xz , do not alter env-file.c, env-util.c or environment-d-generator.c (one env-util.h patch was present; it does not replace the parser functions). The official source's merge_env_file at 557-569 uses this parser. Tagged upstream v255 and v257 carry the same empty-value callback; v233 fileio.c:710-750 also did. Ubuntu/Debian custom image bases are expressly supported by SPEC.md:472-475, with no extra container systemd version floor stated. Thus a supported concrete Ubuntu distribution route exists; no claim that every supported value was refuted remains. The generator discards the assignment, rather than emitting an empty value, on the next user-manager startup. This establishes exact-environment loss; it does not establish a specific network-client fallback or security consequence.

event.summary: Power loss can roll back container ownership before external work
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: a power failure on the helm can lose its most recent ownership/pending records while a remotely created container survives; explicit leftover cleanup may then be needed. This is reachable in production, unlike the initial storage-only revision in interface g064/c3. Exact source: provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:388-398 registers the pending environment via ProviderHandle::register_session; store/podman.rs:355-394 commits that row with ordinary conn.call. podman.rs:1103-1125 writes selected facts/login/pending marker through set_podman_prepared_create (store/podman.rs:256-278, ordinary conn.call) before sending run. Canonical ID is saved through ordinary conn.call at store/podman.rs:415-432. Db::call (farhelm-supervisor/src/db.rs:230-245) does not invoke with_full_sync; configure_durability at 94-117 selects NORMAL in WAL. Process crashes preserve these commits, but power loss can roll them back. Source checks also bound the consequence: create refuses adoption of a name collision without saved ID/pending marker (podman.rs:1073-1077); destroy with neither record returns never_created without a name lookup or rm (1294-1302). A recorded pending lookup pins canonical ID before removal (1306-1319), otherwise a saved ID authorizes only that immutable container. This does not establish accidental deletion of surviving user work. An unregistered surviving container retains helm/role labels and is eligible for explicit leftover discovery/removal at its place; l2 separately obstructs global discovery when an enumerated place fails. Original potential highest consequence retained: a surviving user container could become untracked or unavailable through normal host/session views after its ownership records roll back; direct data deletion is not shown. Suggested bucket: unresolved for the parent's decision; could-be-highest: potentially for loss of access to user-owned processes/work, not an established destructive route. Confidence: confirmed source behavior, not runtime observation. proposed_drop: specification acceptance, requiring independent consideration because of the original possible-highest consequence. Exact cited text in SPEC_impl.md Helm internals, 5668-5672: 'every ordinary read-write connection selects `synchronous=NORMAL` only after reading an actual WAL mode and otherwise retains FULL. This accepts losing the last commits on an OS crash or power loss without weakening database consistency; process crashes preserve commits.' The same section enumerates the trust-revocation writes requiring FULL; these creation ownership writes are not among them. SPEC_impl.md:6682-6685 additionally says for the shared sandbox ownership model, 'A row with neither a saved ID nor an outstanding create is removed without looking up its name or deleting any sandbox or snapshots' and 'A legacy row or a power loss that lost both records cannot recover by name: remove that host entry, then handle the leftover explicitly.' The Container sessions contract reuses sandbox ownership/cleanup rules. SPEC_impl.md:6840-6842 says 'Ordinary write durability is retained: a legacy row or power loss that loses both the ID and pending marker requires explicit cleanup.' Those texts support a proposed accepted tail-loss outcome rather than silently demanding a new FULL barrier. possible_cover: none beyond these cited specifications; prohibited coverage sources were not searched. No tests, builds or reproductions ran.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. Discovery pass2 considered delete_leftover returning success on an absent canonical ID before it reads host/recipe references. TLDR of considered consequence: a request to the rowless cleanup route might bypass whole-host removal and forget registered ownership/session information merely because its supplied resource is absent. Source refutation: the early success at podman.rs:727-729 returns only from the provider cleanup operation. The HTTP handler at876-907 runs that future to completion, bumps FleetEvents and returns an empty JSON success; it contains no host-row/session-cache removal, Destroyed proof or manager forget. The row/reference checks at740-763 reject actually present recorded resources. Registry forgetting uses the separate host removal path, not a shared success tail in this handler. Thus even a direct authenticated request naming an absent ID cannot use this early branch to erase a registered host's ownership or sessions. It is an idempotent absent-leftover receipt only. Suggested bucket if established: potentially highest for losing track of user work through an unauthorized registry-removal path; could-be-highest: yes for that considered consequence, but no such shipped mutation route exists in this handler. Confidence: confirmed source/caller refutation, not runtime observation. proposed_drop: source refutation limited to absent rowless-cleanup success implicitly forgetting a registered host; proposed only for independent parent handling. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this does not claim actual host removal or image retirement has the same effect boundaries, and does not refute known l2 discovery obstruction or g061/l8 recursive image pruning. No tests, builds, reproductions or live-install actions.
